findings.message: The raw-message hidden-information test in tests/integration/fruits.test.ts ("sends a pedestal's kit only to the player moored there who inspects it ...") only reads frames sent after the marks it takes at line 357. By then playersAt() has already joined the players, placed their ships in sight of Palm Key and Mist Cay, and started the match through the lobby. So the first sync of each player's pedestal markers and own status happens before any frame is recorded. For the far player, pedestal-3's marker never changes afterwards, so none of its encoding is ever checked. No integration test scans frames from join (framesSince(0)) for kit names. If the deal leaked into the first sync (a kit field on PedestalMarkerSchema, or in another player's status), no test would fail. Today's schema carries no kit, so this is a gap in the test, not a defect.
findings.requirement: no message to any other player names a pedestal's kit

findings.message: No test shows that a duel fought after a defeat starts with the eater's kit. The test 'refuses a fed player's further attempts and an empty pedestal, and keeps the kit through a lost duel' (tests/integration/fruits.test.ts:274) checks only the status field fruitView().kit === 'ember' after the respawn. It never grapples again to check seaDuelDiagnostics(...).kits or the lobby's kits in a later duel. The only duel-kit test (line 314) checks the eater's first duel.
findings.requirement: The eaten kit replaces the player's two specials (U, I) in every sea duel for the rest of the match, including after a defeat.
